children: Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co., Ltd. Sponsored ADR (TWSE:2330) projected strong Q4 margins and revenue while ramping 2nm/3nm production—including Nvidia NVHBM dies and a second Kumamoto 3nm plant—boosting AI capacity, equipment spend and strategic sourcing amid DoD interest and mixed talks with Elon Musk.
: TSMC (2330) guided Q4 revenue $52.3–$54.3B, gross margin 65–67%, operating margin 56.5–58.5% (Q3 was 58.7%). 2nm output drove ~8% of Q3 wafer revenue; ADRs rose ~2.5%.
: TSMC (2330) named foundry for Nvidia's next‑gen NVHBM base dies, to be made on TSMC's 3nm process as Nvidia aims for a common TSMC‑based production route.
: TSMC (2330) will build 3nm chips at its second Kumamoto JASM plant. Equipment spending will top $23B, phased by demand. Facility targets growing AI chip demand in Japan and globally.
: TSMC (2330) is surveying vendors for rare-earth-free motors and substitutes in factory automation to cut reliance on Chinese rare earths; efforts are early-stage with no large-scale adoption yet.
: Pentagon CTO says the DoD is exploring investments in microelectronics suppliers, including Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. (2330), and plans further deals over the next 12 months
: Elon Musk said talks occurred about cooperation with Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Co. (2330), then said Terafab would run the facilities itself, lowering hopes for a formal tie with 2330.
This is an AI-generated summary and may contain inaccuracies. Please verify any important information with the original sources.

title: Weekly Recap: Q4 guidance and 3nm foundry for Nvidia NVHBM
